headline: Markets hold steady into a loaded Fed-and-earnings super week
body: Index futures ticked higher Monday morning as crude oil retreated from last week's spike, giving equities a modestly firmer start to what several trading desks are calling a 'super week': the Fed's rate decision lands Wednesday afternoon alongside a wave of hyperscaler earnings. Futures markets are pricing only a small chance of a hike, with a hold the dominant expectation, so the tone heading into the meeting reads as wait-and-see rather than anxious. Alphabet and Microsoft report Tuesday, with Amazon and Intel following Wednesday, putting AI capital spending back under the microscope just as third-quarter GDP and the September PCE inflation print land later in the week -- a dense calendar that leaves little room for markets to simply drift.

The dominant single narrative remains the AI and semiconductor trade, which has whipsawed for months on competing reads of whether hyperscaler capex is paying off or running ahead of demand -- the same tension investors will be listening for on this week's earnings calls. Retail-sentiment trackers didn't turn up a clear consensus signal today, so this read leans more on the macro calendar and positioning ahead of the Fed than on social chatter. Taken together, the setup looks less like conviction in either direction than a market parked in neutral, waiting on two concrete catalysts -- the rate decision and hyperscaler results -- to decide whether the recent AI-valuation jitters resolve higher or lower.
